summary:
Sam Whitmore and Jason Yuan, co-founders of New Computer, present at the AI Engineer Summit 2023 on rethinking human-computer interaction through intelligence. They frame intelligence as the ability to take in information from multiple sources, reason about it, and react—mirroring the human sense-think-react loop. ChatGPT represented a breakthrough where computers began approximating this loop through language.

They demonstrate several interaction paradigms. A live demo uses camera-based pose detection to dynamically switch input modalities—keyboard/text when close, voice/audio when far—with an LLM as reasoning engine. A speculative social interface envisions AR/VR headsets interpreting social gestures (dismissive wave to decline calls) while accounting for cultural differences. A new physics demo imagines an iPad Midjourney canvas app using physical metaphors—zooming, blending via light, shaking to remix. They emphasize that generative intelligence is a probabilistic material, fluid like fog or mercury, and rigid metaphors like wood or metal may be inappropriate.

A final speculative mixed-reality demo envisions a wearable with camera, microphone, and projection. Users point at objects and speak naturally ("this is cool"), receive projection-mapped feedback, flick away errors like dust instead of pressing undo, and ask contextual questions about their environment. Crucially, they argue that voice in doesn't require voice out, gesture in doesn't require gesture out—modalities can be mixed in real time based on context.

They conclude that many sensors and contextual signals (typing speed, tone of voice) are already available as inputs to LLM reasoning layers, making everything an input and outputs potentially everywhere and every format. They caution designers to be intentional and ground probabilistic interfaces in familiar metaphors from nature, physics, and human-made tools. Social norms also serve as material—a banking AI shouldn't have philosophical conversations. They close by questioning what truly intelligent interfaces might look like beyond current isomorphism with human perception.

takeaways: Intelligence can be framed as a sense-think-react loop that AI interfaces should approximate
Use LLMs as reasoning engines to interpret both explicit inputs (typing, speech) and implicit signals (position, pose, tone, typing speed)
Computers should adapt to human context rather than requiring humans to adapt to computers
Generative intelligence is a probabilistic material—fluid like fog or mercury—requiring non-rigid interaction metaphors
Voice in doesn't require voice out; gesture in doesn't require gesture out—modalities can mix in real time based on context
Ground probabilistic interfaces in familiar metaphors from nature, physics, and human-made tools
Social norms function as a design material—interfaces should match contextual social expectations
Everything can be an input; outputs can be everywhere in every format—but designers must be intentional about appropriate modality
All demos are speculative inspiration pieces, not representative of New Computer's actual product
Understand the sense-think-react framework for designing AI interfaces

sections.title: Introduction and Philosophy of Intelligence
sections.summary: Sam and Jason introduce themselves as co-founders of New Computer, framing intelligence as the ability to take in information, reason, and react. They describe the human sense-think-react loop and note ChatGPT as a turning point where computers began approximating this loop through language input and output.

sections.title: Adaptive Input Modality Demo
sections.summary: Live demo using camera-based pose detection to dynamically switch between keyboard/text and voice/audio modalities based on user proximity to screen. LLM acts as reasoning engine interpreting user position. Demo partially worked with delayed voice response. Takeaway: combine explicit and implicit inputs, use LLM as reasoning engine, adapt to user context.

sections.title: Social Interface (Speculative)
sections.summary: Jason presents a speculative social interface for future headsets with hand and eye tracking. Users could express intent through explicit social gestures (dismissive wave to decline calls) and implicit signals (gesture speed, mood, distance). Cultural norms for gestures must be considered when scaling globally.

sections.title: New Physics Demo (Speculative)
sections.summary: Speculative iPad demo imagining a Midjourney canvas app where users manipulate AI-generated images through physical metaphors: zooming to create space, blending photos via light metaphor inspired by Pink Floyd, and shaking to remix content like a blender bottle. Advocates treating intelligent materials like real physical materials.

sections.title: Mixed Reality Wearable Demo and Closing Takeaways
sections.summary: Speculative demo of a mixed-reality wearable with camera, microphone, and projection. User browses a Beyonce tour book, points at images and says 'this is cool'—device provides projection-mapped feedback. Errors handled physically—flick away wrong selections like dust instead of pressing undo. User asks AI to identify a friend for Halloween plans with projection-mapped UI blending naturally with the world. Key insight: voice in doesn't mean voice out, gesture in doesn't mean gesture out—modalities can mix in real time. Closing takeaways: everything can be an input, outputs can be everywhere in every format; ground probabilistic interfaces in familiar metaphors; social norms function as design material. Closes questioning what truly intelligent interfaces might look like beyond current isomorphism.

demonstrations: Live pose detection demo: camera detects user position relative to screen, LLM switches between keyboard/text and voice/audio modalities based on proximity
Social interface demo (speculative): AR headset with hand/eye tracking interpreting social gestures to decline calls and determine user intent
New physics demo (speculative): iPad Midjourney canvas app using physical metaphors (zoom, blend via light, shake to remix) for manipulating AI-generated images

Mixed reality wearable demo (speculative): wearable with camera, microphone, and projection; user points at objects and speaks, receives projection-mapped feedback, flicks away errors like dust, asks AI contextual questions about environment
limitations: Live demo partially failed—system delayed voice response before eventually responding
Speculative demos assume near-future hardware capabilities (headsets with hand/eye tracking, wearables with projection)
Demos are explicitly stated as inspiration pieces, not representative of actual product
Gesture-based interactions are error-prone, requiring graceful physical recovery mechanisms
quantitativeClaims: iPad has over five daily active users (likely meant millions, possibly misspoken)
